name: document.referrer
plain: Script-readable copy of the Referer, available the moment a page loads.
meaning: Same previous-site data as the header, readable by any script on the page including third-party tags. Tag managers use it to label traffic sources; Safari 26 and Brave can blank it for classified tracker scripts.

access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can tell which page you came from the moment the page loads
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a page loads after you clicked a link
can: Tell which site or page sent you
Use that to credit a campaign, ad or search
Share the origin of the previous page with analytics tools
cannot: See the full address of the previous page for cross site links, by default only the site name
See pages you visited earlier than the last one
Know the search words from most search engines
Know anything if you typed the address or used a bookmark

story.what_it_is: Any script on a page can read which site you came from.

marketing.name: document.referrer
marketing.pitch: Developer docs describe it as the address of the page that linked to the current one.

story.for_you: You never see it. When a page loads, scripts on it, including third party ones, can check where you came from. That may be a search engine, a friend's post or an ad.
story.for_makers: Tag managers use it to label traffic as search, social or ads. Analytics and ad scripts use it for attribution. Because any script can read it, it is also a leak path for details of the page you were on before.

use_cases.example: A blog sees that most readers came from a Reddit post and tags them as social traffic.
An ad script checks if you came from a partner site and then shows that partner's offer.
A shop sees you came from a price comparison site and shows a better coupon.
A login page checks the referrer to spot hits from known phishing sites.
A game site checks if you came from a streamer's page and unlocks a bonus for that creator's fans.
A paywall that checks if you came from a search engine, and lets you read a free article.

risks: Third party scripts can read it too

technical_bounds: Empty on direct visits, bookmarks, typed URLs and rel=noreferrer links
Not available to cross-origin frames beyond what their own request carried

abuse: Cross-site history sniffing by tag vendors

history.change: Advanced Fingerprinting Protection on by default in regular browsing: classified scripts lose access to document.referrer and URL query parameters (per reporting, verify scope)
